extraction.name: OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning
extraction.description: OWSM v4 is a series of fully open speech foundation models trained on 320k hours of curated multilingual speech data. The models support automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD) across 151 languages. The training data includes cleaned YODAS dataset (166k hours across 75 languages) combined with previous OWSM v3.2 data.
extraction.creator: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe
extraction.publisher: Carnegie Mellon University, Honda Research Institute Japan
extraction.citeAs: Yifan Peng, Muhammad Shakeel, Yui Sudo, William Chen, Jinchuan Tian, Chyi-Jiunn Lin, Shinji Watanabe. OWSM v4: Improving Open Whisper-Style Speech Models via Data Scaling and Cleaning. Interspeech 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset combines cleaned YODAS data (166k hours across 75 languages) with previous OWSM v3.2 data, totaling 320k hours. YODAS is a large-scale web-crawled dataset with Creative Commons license. The data collection includes diverse speaking styles and acoustic environments, with unsegmented long-form audio recordings suitable for Whisper-style training.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YODAS (370k hours of audio in 149 languages) web-crawled from the internet, combined with OWSM v3.2 data. YODAS publicly releases audio files in a Creative Commons license instead of links to original sources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-step data-cleaning pipeline: (1) Resegmentation: Realign audio and text using CTC segmentation algorithm with OWSM-CTC v3.2 model. Long-form recordings segmented into shorter utterances with maximum duration of 30 seconds. Utterances consisting exclusively of non-speech elements (e.g., music) are removed. (2) LID-based filtering: Perform language identification on both audio (using ECAPA-TDNN from SpeechBrain) and text (using fastText). Retain only utterances where original language label matches both predicted languages. (3) CTC-score-based filtering: Remove utterances with low-quality audio-text alignments based on CTC confidence scores. A threshold of θCTC = 0.10 is used, ranking scores within each language and discarding entire long-form utterances if any constituent short utterances fall within the lowest quantile. This process reduced data from 345k hours (83 languages) to 166k hours (75 languages).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: YODAS provides text transcriptions annotated with start and end timestamps. These timestamps are realigned using CTC segmentation algorithm with a pre-trained OWSM-CTC v3.2 model to correct inaccuracies.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: CTC confidence scores are calculated during segmentation to quantify alignment quality between audio and text. These scores are language-dependent and used for filtering low-quality data. Utterances are ranked within each language, and a relative threshold (quantile) is applied.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The cleaned YODAS data, pre-trained models, training code, and training logs will be publicly released via the ESPnet toolkit. YODAS establishes a scalable pipeline to crawl data from the web, and future versions can further grow.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution across languages is highly imbalanced. English constitutes the largest share (74.6k hours after filtering at θCTC=0.10), whereas many other languages continue to be underrepresented. The original distribution is kept without any resampling.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The raw YODAS data contains annotation errors including mismatched language labels and misalignment between audio and text. The OWSM-CTC v3.2 model used for resegmentation supports only a subset of languages present in YODAS. The cleaned dataset is highly imbalanced across languages, with English dominating and many languages underrepresented.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training speech foundation models for automatic speech recognition (ASR), speech translation (ST), language identification (LID), and voice activity detection (VAD). The models are evaluated on multilingual ASR benchmarks (FLEURS, MLS, Common Voice), English ASR (Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard), LID (FLEURS), and speech translation (CoVoST-2).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OWSM-CTC v3.2 model for CTC segmentation and confidence score calculation, ECAPA-TDNN from SpeechBrain for spoken language identification, fastText for text-based language identification
